prompt: a colour field sketch of a single bird, as a birder would draw it from life and finish in the studio: a light pencil underdrawing carrying clean watercolour washes and coloured-pencil detail, worked up sharply where identification lives — head, bill, eye, wing pattern, the edges of each feather tract — and left looser and more sketchy toward the tail, belly and legs, a few pencil strokes still showing; true proportions and a faithful likeness of the species, natural unsaturated colours, soft daylight; the bird alone on plain white paper, no border, no caption, no text. A Azure Tit (Cyanistes cyanus), perched on a small branch, wings folded neatly against the body, side profile. Identification — emphasise these field marks: Small white-and-blue tit with a clean white head, an azure-blue crown-band through the eye, blue wings with a white wing-bar, blue tail, and white underparts. Tiny dark bill, blue-grey legs. Render the legs and feet accurately: legs and feet typical of the species, both clearly shown and not cut off. Keep the likeness of the bird in the reference photo: same proportions, bill and head shape, posture, plumage pattern and colour tones — a portrait of this species, not a generic or idealised bird. Draw the bird only: leave out everything around it in the photo — habitat, foliage, branches, grass, water, sky, rocks, snow, fences, wires, feeders, hands, rings, other birds — on plain white, no cast shadow, no backdrop; at most the barest neutral perch under its feet. A typical wild adult in natural, muted colours, the whole bird in frame, uncropped, both legs and feet visible. anatomically correct, exactly two wings in a natural realistic position with properly layered flight feathers, correct wing orientation, natural posture.
